title: Molecular Entanglement and Electrospinnability of Biopolymers
protocol: Prepare a range of biopolymer concentrations from 0.1% to 30%, w/v.
Weigh the biopolymer powder into a 50 ml test tube.
Add aqueous dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) solution and a stir bar to the test tube.
Place the test tube in boiling water with constant stirring on a magnetic stirrer hotplate for about 1 hour.
Turn off heat and allow the dispersion to cool to room temperature.
Warm up the rheometer and set the stage temperature at 20 °C.
Calibrate the gap between the probe (25 mm cone used) and the stage (plate).
Load 0.41 ml of the biopolymer dispersion onto the center of the stage.
Lower the probe to set the position with a 0.053 mm gap for the 25 mm cone.
Ensure that the dispersion evenly spreads within the gap.

Perform the rheological test with log sweep mode, initial rate: 100 sec-1, final rate: 0.1 sec-1, points per decade: 10, delay before measure: 5 sec, measure time: 10 sec, and directions per measure: two (both clockwise and counterclockwise).
Analyze rheological data to estimate appropriate dispersion concentrations for electrospinning trials.
Plot apparent shear viscosities against shear rates as a function of polymer concentrations.
Approximate zero shear viscosities by actual or extrapolated values at low shear rate data unreliable points.
Calculate specific viscosity using the formula ηsp = (η0− ηs)/ηs, where ηs is the viscosity of the solvent.
Plot specific viscosities as a function of concentration.
Identify semidilute unentangled and entangled regimes in the plot.
Fit power-law regression models for both semidilute unentangled and entangled regimes on log-log plots.
Determine the entanglement concentration, ce, from the intersection of the two fitted lines.
Assemble the electrospinning setup as shown in Figure 1.
Load the syringe with dispersion of appropriate composition onto the syringe pump.
Clip the high voltage wire (positive) to the needle.
Connect the coagulation bath containing pure ethanol to ground by immersing the ground wire into the bath.
Use a lab jack to adjust the distance between the syringe needle and coagulation bath.
Immerse a metal mesh in the bath to collect the fiber mat after electrospinning.
Spin the biopolymer with feed rate from 0.1 to 0.4 ml/hr, spinning distance from 5 to 10 cm, and voltage from 0 to 15 kV.
Start with a spinning distance of 5 cm.
Ramp the voltage up slowly from 0 V for the first feed rate (0.1 ml/hr).
Note when the dripping dispersion is accelerated and then elongated at the needle tip.
Record the voltage at which a tiny jet initiated from the drop surface, indicating electrospinnability of the solution.
Examine the complete range for each of the three parameters and note successful spinning conditions.
Collect the fibers only when there is a continuous jet from the tip.
Rinse the fiber mat with pure ethanol after a few minutes of collecting.
Place the fiber mat into a desiccator containing desiccant under vacuum.
Cut a piece of dried fiber mat and immobilize it onto a SEM stub using carbon tape.
Load the sample stub into the SEM instrument and obtain images for analysis.
